summary: Embedding shard merge introduced extraneous padding bytes; reranker dropping candidates and causing p99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent loss of reranker candidates and large p99 latency spikes after a daily shard maintenance window.

Impact: NimbusDocs sees ~7% of queries return fewer-than-expected top-k results and p99 tail latency for their /rerank endpoint increased from ~120ms to ~1.3s during a 30m window. This affects search relevance and user experience for their dedicated cluster.

Environment: prod dedicated cluster (us-east), dedicated capacity, embedding ingestion pipeline writes to shard groups S-14..S-18 during the maintenance merge job.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a manual shard-merge on a replica set containing 3 rotated segments (simulated via staging script).
2) Submit batch embedding+rerank flow used by NimbusDocs (256-dim embeddings, batch size 64).
3) Observe rerank responses and token-level metrics; compare before/after merge.

Observed behavior: Merged embedding payloads include extra zero-padding bytes appended to the end of the serialized vector. The reranker receives vectors with inconsistent effective dimension metadata and rejects or drops candidates in the ANN stage, while some requests fall back to CPU-based brute-force scanning causing p99 latency spike.

Expected behavior: Shard merge should produce compact, canonical embedding payloads with matching dimension headers. Reranker should receive consistent vectors and return deterministic top-k without fallback for this workload.

Initial customer-provided logs: Attached trace id t-20260312-9f3a (included in comments). Customer also provided a sample merged payload (hex) showing 16 trailing 0x00 bytes.

Temporary workaround: Disabled shard auto-merge for NimbusDocs' namespace until a fix is deployed. Recommended customer-side mitigation: pin to older shard snapshot or route rerank to fallback model alias.

Notes on urgency: Customer is in active production and relies on consistent rerank results for their SLAs. Priority set to P1 and Sev1 assigned.

investigation_notes: Binary serializer writes a padding alignment buffer for historical reasons (optimizing page writes) but merge path omitted header-length recalculation in ~20% of runs due to a race when merging odd-numbered segments.
The reranker validates expected_dim header against payload length; mismatch triggers ANN index to drop candidates rather than erroring loudly, which is causing silent top-k loss.
CPU fallback path is invoked when the ANN engine returns empty candidate set; this explains p99 spike observed concurrently with dropped candidates.

Canary mitigation implemented at proxy layer: detect length mismatch, trim trailing 0x00 bytes, and rewrite dimension header before forwarding. This is a short-term bandaid while embedding-service hotfix is reviewed.
Root cause traced to commit 3b7d9a2 (storage: add alignment buffer) which did not update merge_writer metadata handling for odd-segment merges.

Proposed permanent fix: patch merge_writer to recompute and write correct header after padding, add unit/integration test for odd-size merges, and add an observability metric for "padding_trimmed_count".
resolution: Mitigation: proxy-level trimming was deployed to canary (10%) on 2026-03-14 and expanded after positive signals. Permanent fix is implemented in PR #1428 (embedding-service) and currently in code review. Post-deploy plan: deploy fix to production, backfill affected shard merges for NimbusDocs during a maintenance window, run regression test suite for shard merges, and add monitoring alert for "merge_padding_detected". Customer accepted mitigation and requested a postmortem after deployment. Follow-up tasks: INT-33421 created to add integration tests and retention metrics.
